newsitem.title: USA: CBOT rice soars to higher close on exports.
newsitem.headline: CBOT rice soars to higher close on exports.

text.p: CBOT rice futures ended sharply higher, buoyed by strong exports, tight domestic supplies and fund buying, analysts and traders said.

USDA early Thursday said U.S. net export sales of rice totaled 70,500 tonnes. That tally was 42 percent below the previous week but 29 percent above the four-week average sales pace, according to USDA.
Traders said the previous week's sales total was an unusually strong number so Thursday's figure for trade last week was a bullish surprise.
"This rice market is underpinned by two things, large export demand for U.S. long grain rice and tight domestic supply," Rice Market Advisory Letter publisher J.P. Gaines said.
Traders also said there was talk Colombia would tender for 15,000 to 30,000 tonnes of paddy rice.
Rice futures trading volume was heavy early but tapered off late in the session in fast trading.
March rice settled at $12.39 per cwt, a new contract high and up the 30-cent limit.
Dean Witter Reynolds senior vice president, futures Neauman Coleman noted brisk fund buying early through Dean Witter and LIT America.
